builds.name: Reference: Spell-and-attack
builds.goal: Reference for Twisted Fate: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A ranged pick-and-roam mage who selects a card for control or mana, then uses map vision and teleport to create numbers advantages. His attack cadence also produces periodic Stacked Deck damage. Select the actual card and fix Stacked Deck cadence. Attack-speed builds trade spell burst for repeated real attacks; gold-card safety and roaming time matter. Real empowered attacks may cash Lich Bane while AP strengthens compatible spells.
builds.summary: Real empowered attacks may cash Lich Bane while AP strengthens compatible spells.
testPlan: Kit question for Twisted Fate: Select the actual card and fix Stacked Deck cadence. Attack-speed builds trade spell burst for repeated real attacks; gold-card safety and roaming time matter.

Start with the early core (Lich Bane, then Nashor only if attacks pay off) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Real empowered attacks may cash Lich Bane while AP strengthens compatible spells. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Twisted Fate throws three cards, dealing damage to each enemy unit they pass through. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Spells without on-hit delivery do not consume Spellblade; stepping into attack range costs uptime.

The route fails Twisted Fate's stated kit question: Select the actual card and fix Stacked Deck cadence. Attack-speed builds trade spell burst for repeated real attacks; gold-card safety and roaming time matter.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Spells without on-hit delivery do not consume Spellblade; stepping into attack range costs uptime.
Full cost 16,650 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Lich Bane, then Nashor only if attacks pay off. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff, Zhonya's Hourglass are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Blue card crit hybrid
builds.summary: Test blue card crit hybrid against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test blue card crit hybrid against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Blue Card has 1.0 AP and total-AD magic damage plus an explicit crit-chance contribution; Infinity Edge tests that documented critical-damage term, not ordinary spell crit. Rapid Firecannon extends one energized attack while Lich Bane adds an independent magic packet; Statikk retains hybrid attack pressure.
testPlan: Required state: Lock Blue Card with an energized attack and a safe angle.
Measure blue, red and gold cards at matched AP with varied crit stats.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: No Gold Card stun and no percent magic penetration limit safety and tank damage.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: The W formula is a special modifier, not proof Wild Cards randomly crits.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Infinity Edge, Rapid Firecannon, Lich Bane, Rabadon's Deathcap, Statikk Shiv, Berserker's Greaves. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.summary: Test destiny on-hit pursuit against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test destiny on-hit pursuit against conventional damage at equal gold.

testPlan: Required state: Arrive safely through R and lock a Gold Card before firing.
Count E procs and Hexplate uptime through R reveal and teleport.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.

The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.

Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
